articles.title: Teacher shortages strain government primary schools
articles.excerpt: Government primary schools across Bangladesh are struggling to keep lessons on track as headteacher posts remain vacant in more than half of the institutions while thousands of assistant-teacher positions also remain unfilled.

articles.title: Honouring a trailblazer
articles.excerpt: More than five decades ago, Niloufer Manzur set out to establish a school that would provide children with a strong academic foundation while developing their conscience and sense of responsibility towards their country.

articles.title: Admission test woes of first graders
articles.excerpt: The government's move to reintroduce written admission tests for class-1 from the next academic year has sparked concern among parents, with many turning to coaching centres and private tutors.

articles.title: When calling Messi GOAT is no longer enough
articles.excerpt: Until the 85th minute of Thursday's semifinal, Argentina were trailing England by a goal, and a spot in the final seemed to be slipping away.

articles.title: UGC to track 15 years of university research funding
articles.excerpt: The University Grants Commission is preparing a research repository to track how university research funds were spent and what they produced over the past 15 years.

articles.title: Draft guidelines signal new direction for primary curriculum
articles.excerpt: Draft guidelines for updating the primary curriculum suggest defining what children should know and the skills and competencies they should attain by the end of class-5.

articles.title: Education outlay rises sharply
articles.excerpt: The new budget proposed a sharp increase in education spending, while experts cautioned that a larger allocation would matter only if it translated into better learning outcomes.

articles.title: Education, health outlay to rise 63%
articles.excerpt: The government is set to place education and health at the centre of its spending plan, with the combined allocation for the two sectors likely to rise sharply.
